about: Free-fall (brake) periodic orbits for the reversibility diagnostic (validation::reversibility, the gate reversibility-xi). Each row is copied digit for digit from Hristov, Hristova, Dmitrasinovic & Tanikawa, 'Three-body periodic collisionless equal-mass free-fall orbits revisited', Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 136, 7 (2024), doi:10.1007/s10569-023-10177-w, arXiv:2308.16159 (CC BY 4.0), database https://db2.fmi.uni-sofia.bg/3bodyfree/, file sol_80.txt (committed at docs/incoming/2026-10-27_hp_ics_freefall/data/sofia_3bodyfree/sol_80.txt, sha256 81dc1b70828fd5960dec57f64ac88f7945fa5c8eddf1cfb6ea33b3475c55373c), its 1-based line 'row'. Published by the authors; included as test data with citation; not ours.
convention: G = 1, equal masses m = 1, all three bodies at rest at t = 0 at r1 = (-1/2, 0), r2 = (1/2, 0), r3 = (x, y). 'period' is T, the period; 'scaled_period' is T* = T |E|^(3/2), the database's ordering key. Checked on each row by validation::reversibility's tests: T* recomputed from (x, y, T) agrees with the file's to 1e-12 relative.
chosen: The three rows of least T* that are distinct orbits: rows 1 and 2 of sol_80.txt share T* to all 80 digits (14.3613...), as do rows 4 and 5 (15.5834...): one orbit read at each of its two brake configurations, so rows 2 and 5 are left out. Row 3 is also the first self-dual solution (sd_80.txt row 1). Least T* first, because the shortest orbits take the fewest steps and are expected to amplify round-off least over one period.
